transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I feel like my feelings and motivation have dried up; it’s getting harder to connect with my clients or even with my own life. I used to be so passionate about my social work, but now I just feel fundamentally shut down inside and can't seem to shake it.
Do you find that these feelings of being shut down and lacking motivation are mostly tied to your work, or do they affect your personal life and things you used to enjoy outside of work as well?

It definitely affects my whole life, not just work. I've stopped doing things I used to love like yoga, art outings, and seeing my friends, and now I just spend my evenings alone ignoring phone calls. Even basic chores like buying groceries and cleaning feel too heavy to manage right now.
How long have you been feeling this way, and did these symptoms start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

The heavy, shut-down feeling and the decline in my life have been building for about eight months, starting around the time my clinic caseload got overwhelming and my aunt's health issues intensified. However, those newer, unsettling feelings—like sensing that people at work and the hospital are secretly evaluating me—have only been happening for the last two months.
When you feel that people are secretly evaluating you, do you ever actually hear voices whispering or talking about you when no one is around, or see things that others don't?

No, I don't hear any voices whispering or see things that others don't. It's more that I'm picking up on hints and messages in emails, staff meetings, and people's behavior that make me feel like I'm being secretly evaluated.
Have you ever experienced these feelings of being secretly evaluated or watched during a time when your mood was completely fine and you weren't feeling depressed?

No, I have never felt like I was being watched or evaluated at any other point in my life. These thoughts only started about two months ago, which was long after I already felt completely flat and shut down, which began about eight months ago.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are not your own, such as being put into your mind by an outside force, or that others can read your mind?

No, I have never felt like my thoughts were being controlled or put into my head by an outside force. I also don't feel like anyone else can read my mind. My thoughts are still my own, even if I feel completely shut down inside.
Have you ever had periods in your life lasting several days where you felt the exact opposite—unusually energetic, needing very little sleep, or feeling like your thoughts were racing?

No, I've never had periods of high energy or racing thoughts like that. In fact, my experience has been the exact opposite. I mostly just feel heavy, flat, and completely lacking in any energy or drive.
Have you ever experienced a similar period of feeling deeply depressed, flat, or losing interest in things at any other time in your past, before these last eight months?
No, I have never felt this way before. This level of feeling completely "shut down" and losing my drive is entirely new to me, having only started over the last eight months.
During this difficult time, have you been experiencing strong feelings of worthlessness or guilt, or have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or that life is no longer worth living?

No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself, and I don't really feel guilty or worthless. It is more that I just feel completely blank, heavy, and numb inside. It's like my emotions have been turned all the way down, rather than me feeling actively suicidal.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with an eight-month history of a severe depressive episode characterized by profound emotional flatness, severe anhedonia, loss of drive, and social withdrawal. Two months ago, she developed mood-congruent psychotic symptoms, specifically delusions of reference and persecution (believing colleagues are secretly evaluating her and finding hidden messages in emails and meetings). These psychotic symptoms occur exclusively within the context of the depressive episode. There is no history of hypomanic/manic episodes or prior psychiatric illness, establishing the diagnosis of a severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms (F32.3).
